chunks: Article 14. Equality before law. The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Finance Commission and fiscal imbalances
sources.publisher: MarkMyWords (summary of constitutional provisions and Finance Commission practice)
chunks: Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because the Union raises a larger share of revenue while States bear a large share of expenditure responsibilities. The Finance Commission recommends the share of States in the divisible pool of central taxes to narrow this gap.

Horizontal imbalance refers to differences in fiscal capacity among States. The Finance Commission distributes the States' share among them using a formula with criteria such as population, area, income distance and other indicators chosen by each Commission.

States have raised concerns that cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, which reduces the effective share of central revenue devolved to them, and that some criteria can penalise States that have controlled population growth.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Sarkaria and Punchhi Commissions
chunks: The Sarkaria Commission (set up in 1983) and the Punchhi Commission (set up in 2007) examined Centre-State relations. Both recommended that Article 356 be used sparingly, only as a last resort after other options are exhausted.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Flexible inflation targeting and transmission
sources.publisher: MarkMyWords (summary of RBI Act provisions and RBI practice)
chunks: Under the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Central Government sets the inflation target in consultation with the RBI, and a six-member Monetary Policy Committee decides the policy repo rate. The target is 4 per cent CPI inflation with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 per cent; it was first notified for 2016-2021 and retained for 2021-2026 and, in March 2026, for 2026-2031. Failure is defined as average inflation outside the band for three consecutive quarters.

Monetary transmission can be slow because banks' cost of funds depends on deposit rates that reprice only as deposits mature, because rates on small savings schemes compete with bank deposits, and because stressed balance sheets and liquidity conditions affect how banks pass on rate changes.

To improve transmission, the RBI moved from the base rate to the marginal cost of funds based lending rate (MCLR) in 2016 and required banks to link certain new floating-rate loans to an external benchmark such as the policy repo rate from October 2019.

heuristic_checks.quote: 4 per cent CPI inflation with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 per cent
heuristic_checks.note: The notified target has been 4% CPI inflation (±2%). Verify the target currently in force.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Goods and Services Tax
sources.publisher: MarkMyWords (summary of constitutional amendment and GST practice)
chunks: The Goods and Services Tax was enabled by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 and rolled out on 1 July 2017. Article 279A created the GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister with State Finance Ministers as members, which recommends rates and rules. States were promised compensation for revenue shortfalls for five years.

heuristic_checks.note: GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017 (the enabling amendment was passed in 2016).
The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Minimum Support Prices
chunks: Minimum Support Prices are announced by the Government on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices. Effective procurement has historically been concentrated in rice and wheat in a few States, which has encouraged these crops over pulses and oilseeds and added to groundwater stress in some regions.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Unified Payments Interface
chunks: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI), operated by the National Payments Corporation of India, was launched in 2016. It enables real-time interoperable payments between bank accounts using a mobile phone and has lowered the cost of accepting digital payments for small merchants.

India has announced a goal of net zero emissions by 2070.

sources.title: MarkMyWords summary — Disaster Management Act, 2005
chunks: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 created the National Disaster Management Authority, chaired by the Prime Minister, along with State and District Disaster Management Authorities, and provided for the National Disaster Response Force.

The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 emphasises understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in resilience and improving preparedness, marking a shift from response to risk reduction.
